items.title: Karnataka High Court strikes down law enhancing SC/ST reservation as total quota exceeds 50% cap
items.summary: The Karnataka High Court on Monday struck down the provisions of the Karnataka Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Reservation of Seats in Educational Institutions and of Appointments or Posts in the Services under the State) Act, 2022, which increased reservation for Scheduled Castes (SCs) from 15 to 17 percent and for Scheduled Tribes (STs) from 3 to 7 percent [Mahendra Kumar Mitra & others Vs Union of India & others]. A bench of Chief Justice Vibhu Bakhru and Justice K S Hemalekha held that Section 3 of the Act, insofar as it took the aggregate reservation beyond the 50 percent ceiling, violated Articles 14 and 15 of the Constitution. The Court also struck down Section 4, which provided for the enhanced reservation in State government services. The plea has sought production of the Election Commission of India's (ECI) internal records on the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls, an independent audit of voter deletions and an interim suspension of the exercise across States. items.summary: Shardul Amarchand Mangaldas & Co has announced the joining of Jithin M. George as a Partner in its Intellectual Property (IP) practice, with effect from October 12, 2026. George is a graduate of Bharati Vidyapeeth, Pune He is an IP litigation specialist with over 12 years of experience handling complex trademark, copyright, geographical indication (GI) and technology-related disputes for multinational and domestic clients. He regularly appears before the Delhi High Court, district courts and other judicial forums across India in infringement, passing-off, rectification and appellate proceedings. He advises clients on enforcement strategy, settlement negotiations, dispute-risk management and IP portfolio protection, and is known for mentoring associates on drafting, case strategy and courtroom advocacy. George joins SAM from K&S Partners, where he spent over seven years leading litigation strategy and case management in high-value contentious matters. items.title: Over 20 journalists recount the Delhi Police’s use of brute force against them
items.summary: As Delhi witnessed a wave of protests against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar, the Delhi Police and the CRPF, deployed to maintain law and order, came down heavily on journalists covering the demonstrations. Journalists were detained and assaulted, their equipment was damaged, and their phones were taken away. In fact, several journalists were detained by the Delhi Police even after a Supreme Court order on the afternoon of October 11 clearly stated that lawyers, journalists, and other professionals “shall not be hindered in the discharge of their professional duties in any manner whatsoever.” The News Minute spoke to around 20 journalists who covered the protests, several of them from digital media organisations. They were demanding the scrapping of the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls and the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. Photojournalists Pushkar V of Deccan Herald and Syed Asif of The Times of India were also allegedly manhandled. Pushkar was manhandled and beaten by four police personnel. According to a press note issued by the organisers, three other journalists were manhandled. Eyewitnesses also stated that women protesters were also severely manhandled by the police. The organisers alleged that police confiscated placards before detaining protesters, some of whom had not yet begun marching. The protesters had gathered to condemn the police action against demonstrators, lawyers, journalists and youth activists in Delhi on October 10. The organisers alleged that police personnel pushed and dragged protesters into buses, beat young people and pulled at the clothes of women protesters. The plea has sought contempt action for the alleged breach, identification of the police officers and supervising officials responsible and disclosure of how the Court’s direction was communicated to personnel deployed on the ground.
